description: Born in Nancy to a family of artists, Clodion was one of the leading French sculptors of the ancien régime and Napoleonic era. He went to Paris to study sculpture in 1755 and worked in Rome from 1767 to 1771.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: An invention of European artists of the post-Roman period, a satyress is the female equivalent of the male satyr in classical antiquity. Part human and part goat or horse, the satyress can be recognized by her animal legs and hoofs.

title: Mural Fragment with Elite Male and Maguey Cactus Leaves
culture: Central Mexico, Tlacuilapaxco apartment compound(?), Teotihuacán style, Classic Period

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2366px open-access image (region x=0.2126, y=0.2008, w=0.2, h=0.2156)

description: This richly dressed elite male belonged to a row of identical figures who processed along the walls of a patio in one of Teotihuacán’s wealthy apartment compounds. He offers a chant or prayer, materialized in a mouth scroll, along with a flower-filled libation that cascades from one hand. In the other hand, he carries an incense bag.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
tags: Central Mexico, Tlacuilapaxco apartment compound(?), Teotihuacán style, Classic Period
interestingFacts: This fragment is from a larger composition that covered the walls of a patio at Teotihuacan.

title: La Cervara, the Roman Campagna
artistBio: Camille Corot's earlier biographers presented him as a naive artist separated from commercial concerns who painted whatever pleased him in the French countryside and from his own emotions. For these writers his importance lay in his loosely painted, atmospheric landscapes, for which later modernists called him the precursor to impressionism.

artistBioSource.name: Cleveland Museum of Art — artist biography

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2438px open-access image (region x=0.6126, y=0.4537, w=0.3, h=0.3138)

description: Corot based his large oil painting on drawings and oil sketches made outdoors. Attracted to the beauty of the Italian countryside, he often sketched around Rome, where he lived from 1825 to 1828.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: In 1845, the French poet Charles Baudelaire proclaimed Corot the leading painter of the modern landscape.

title: Esther, Ahasuerus, and Haman

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2564px open-access image (region x=0.1459, y=0.3452, w=0.3, h=0.2984)

description: Esther, the wife of the Persian king Ahasuerus, effectively concealed her Jewish identity until the prime minister Haman hatched a plot to annihilate the kingdom’s Jews. To save her people Esther persuades the king (at the center) to rescind his order. He then turns against Haman, who slumps in his seat, aware of his sudden fall from power and his bleak future.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: At the center of this biblical scene, Steen included elements of a typical Dutch still life: a Roemer glass, a half-peeled lemon, and a blue-and-white porcelain dish.

title: Sheet of Sketches (recto and verso)
medium: pen and brown ink on ivory laid paper

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x1107px open-access image (region x=0.0959, y=0.1283, w=0.3, h=0.692)

description: The inscription at the upper left of the sheet states that Géricault executed these studies at the spring of the Magdelaine, near the forest of Fontainebleau, which he visited in 1819. The male figures closely resemble the earlier studies he made while in Italy of peasants during horse races at annual Roman carnivals. Here, men struggle to keep control of their unseen animals during the moments before the race.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Géricault died at a young age and had a professional career lasting only just over a decade.

title: Portrait of a Child (Anton Peschka Jr.)

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2215x3400px open-access image (region x=0.1603, y=0.6103, w=0.3011, h=0.1479)

description: Egon Schiele depicted a small child, the son of a friend, in this drawing devoid of setting. The child teeters at an awkward angle, seemingly unsupported but for a multipatterned fabric wrap that occupies the artist’s primary interest.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: The child seen in this drawing, Anton Peschka Jr., served as a model for several compositions by Egon Schiele.

title: Panoramic View of the Alps, Les Dents du Midi
alternativeTitles: Grand Panorama of the Alps with the Dents du Midi
artistBio: Born into a wealthy farmer's family, Courbet began his training in 1831 at the Petit Séminaire in Ornans where, beginning in 1833, he studied under "le père Baud," who had been a pupil of Gros. He was befriended by poet Max Buchon, who would later write the first article on Courbet, claiming that he was the artist for the people.

artistBioSource.name: Cleveland Museum of Art — artist biography

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2428px open-access image (region x=0.1291, y=0.4518, w=0.4209, h=0.4432)

description: Courbet was still working on this large landscape, intended for the Paris Universal Exposition of 1879, when he died in December 1877. He painted it during his exile in Switzerland, where he had fled after being condemned for subversive activities in the Paris Commune of 1871. The view looks south over Lake Geneva toward the mountains called Les Dents du Midi.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: This late, unfinished painting reveals some of Courbet's techniques. At the top of the mountains you can see how different brushstrokes and thickly applied paint were used to differentiate the texture of the clouds from the snow.

title: Portrait of the Jester Calabazas

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2089x3400px open-access image (region x=0.3863, y=0.1312, w=0.4203, h=0.1938)

description: Calabazas, a jester in the court of King Philip IV of Spain, had physical and mental disabilities, a state that the artist emphasizes, rather than tries to hide. While the Spanish court prized and doted upon people with disabilities such as Calabazas, Velázquez transformed their depiction in portraiture.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Calabazas holds a wind-driven pinwheel and a miniature portrait of a woman, together suggesting the inconstancy of love.

title: Twilight in the Wilderness

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2123px open-access image (region x=0.4459, y=0.5082, w=0.3, h=0.3613)

description: In his New York studio, Church painted this spectacular view of a blazing sunset over wilderness near Mount Katahdin in Maine, which he had sketched during a visit nearly two years earlier. Although Church often extolled the grandeur of American landscape in his work, this painting appears to have additional overtones.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: An image of this painting has a cameo in the Harrison Ford film Clear and Present Danger.

title: Memento Mori, "To This Favour"

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2528px open-access image (region x=0.3291, y=0.7089, w=0.2, h=0.2017)

description: The Latin term memento mori describes a traditional subject in art that addresses mortality. In Harnett’s example, the extinguished candle, spent hourglass, and skull symbolize death. A quote from William Shakespeare’s Hamlet, inscribed on the inside cover of a tattered book, reinforces the theme.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Harnett’s family left Ireland during the potato famine and emigrated to the United States.

title: Jonah Swallowed

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2542x3400px open-access image (region x=0.2313, y=0.4541, w=0.3009, h=0.1688)

description: After disobeying the Lord’s command to proclaim judgment on the city of Nineveh, the Old Testament prophet Jonah was cast into the sea and swallowed by a sea monster. Here, the beast swallows Jonah headfirst.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Although usually thought of as a whale, here the artist has depicted Jonah swallowed by a cetus, a large, monstrous sea creature.

title: Laban Searching for His Stolen Household Gods
alternativeTitles: Laban Searching for His Stolen Household Gods in Rachel's Tent

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2259px open-access image (region x=0.6126, y=0.3807, w=0.3, h=0.3395)

description: This story comes from the Old Testament book of Genesis and stresses the value of reconciliation. Jacob lived with his uncle Laban for years, marrying Laban’s daughters Rachel and Leah. When the relationship between the men soured, Jacob and his family departed, while Rachel secretly stole her father’s household gods.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)

title: Arm of Eve
medium: point of brush and gray and black wash, brush and gray and black wash, heightened with white gouache

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2719x3400px open-access image (region x=0.4884, y=0.2291, w=0.4204, h=0.2521)

description: Arm of Eve is the only surviving preparatory drawing for Dürer’s life-size panels of Adam and Eve in the Museo del Prado, Madrid. It is also one of the few surviving drawings by the artist made on Venetian blue paper, a support he began to use for his chiaroscuro studies while visiting Venice in the winter of 1506–7.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: The blue paper that Dürer used to make this drawing was a specialty of Venetian paper makers in the 16th century, who achieved the color by infusing the paper pulp with dyed fibers.

title: Portrait of Genio C. Scott

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2742px open-access image (region x=0.5124, y=0.2662, w=0.2, h=0.186)

description: Eastman Johnson portrayed Genio Scott (1806–1879) as a gentleman of means wearing an informal, yet stylish robe in his New York residence. Scott had a successful career as a women’s fashion illustrator and magazine publisher, but his true passion was fly-fishing.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Genio Scott's detailed writings describing 19th-century fish distribution remain highly useful for present-day conservationists.

title: Silenus

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2603px open-access image (region x=0.1459, y=0.2317, w=0.3, h=0.2943)

description: Before a large wine barrel, Silenus (Bacchus’s teacher) lies inebriated on the ground as he raises his cup to receive wine from a satyr in this print. Jusepe de Ribera included these and other details indicating that the scene was intended to be humorous. Two infants mimic Silenus, and a braying donkey adds to the chaotic setting.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Corpulent bodies were often used in early modern art to symbolize laziness, overindulgence, and moral corruption.

title: Portrait of Infante Don Luis de Borbon

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2204x3400px open-access image (region x=0.3217, y=0.5271, w=0.4211, h=0.2041)

description: As a younger child of King Philip V of Spain, Don Luis received important religious posts, including Archbishop of Toledo and Seville. However, his philandering led to losing these titles and banishment from the court, while he became a crucial avant-garde art patron, especially of Goya.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)

title: The Vicarello Goblet
culture: Italy, Vicarello (ancient Aquae Apollinares), Roman, Augustan period

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2958x3400px open-access image (region x=0.2637, y=0.2688, w=0.2999, h=0.1959)

description: This masterpiece of the Roman silversmith’s art is exquisitely worked in relief. The multifigure scene centers on a rustic shrine of the ithyphallic fertility god Priapus, son of Dionysos. He takes the form of a stylized boundary marker atop a column, where a woman seems to have brought him to life by touching him.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
tags: Italy, Vicarello (ancient Aquae Apollinares), Roman, Augustan period
interestingFacts: This silver cup was found north of Rome at Vicarello (ancient Aquae Apollinares), probably in 1862.

title: Landscape with a Windmill

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2451px open-access image (region x=0.4459, y=0.2195, w=0.3, h=0.3121)

description: Even this early work by Jacob van Ruisdael—painted while he was still a teenager—shows his unique approach to landscape that made the simplest motifs seem grand and heroic. Dark forms are massed in the foreground, creating a stark contrast to the expansive, sunlit plain at left.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Look closely at the field across from the windmill: white linens are naturally bleached in the sun, a process that would have taken several months.

title: Front Face of a Stela (Free-standing Stone with Relief)
culture: Mesoamerica, Guatemala, Department of the Petén, El Perú (also known as Waka'), Maya (250-900), Classic period (200-1000)

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2328x3400px open-access image (region x=0.6869, y=0.5688, w=0.2006, h=0.1041)

description: In stone sculpture, Maya rulers celebrated the milestones of their reigns with flamboyant portraits like this image of a royal woman, created to mark the passage of a twenty-year period known as the k’atun. She originally stood in a plaza next to a portrait of her spouse (see photo), with whom she ruled El Perú-Waka’, a provincial Maya town.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
tags: Mesoamerica, Guatemala, Department of the Petén, El Perú (also known as Waka'), Maya (250-900), Classic period (200-1000)
interestingFacts: The powerful Maya queen shown on this stela is known as Lady K’abel.

title: Low Waterfall in a Wooded Landscape with a Dead Beech Tree

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2565px open-access image (region x=0.1459, y=0.3232, w=0.3, h=0.2982)

description: Jutting from a dune in the foreground, the massive silvery trunk of a dead tree leads the eye across a waterfall and toward a distant sunlit field where travelers and a dog traverse a sandy path. Partly masked by trees, a ruined building is turned gold by the sun. In Jacob van Ruisdael’s landscapes, dead trees, waterfalls, and ruined buildings were visual expressions of the passage of time.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Jacob van Ruisdael was inspired by trees in various states of decay, observed from nature.

title: Terpsichore Lyran (Muse of Lyric Poetry)
alternativeTitles: Terpsichore, Muse of Choral Song and Dance

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2598x3400px open-access image (region x=0.4561, y=0.2041, w=0.3006, h=0.1729)

description: In Greek mythology, Terpsichore was one of the nine Muses, or goddesses of creative inspiration. The lyre, the Greek inscription on the short column, and the caduceus (entwined snakes) on the side identify the figure as Terpsichore Lyran, muse of lyric poetry. This sculpture began with a commission from Napoleon's brother, Lucien, for an idealized portrait of his wife, Alexandrine.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Trained by his grandfather, an Italian stonemason, Canova began modeling clay and carving marble sculptures before age ten.

title: Standing Buddha

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 1950x3400px open-access image (region x=0.6072, y=0.8082, w=0.2, h=0.0853)

description: This bronze Buddha is exceptional, because it carries an inscription on its base that dates its manufacture to the year 591. According to the inscription, the sculpture was dedicated by a nun who was from a village in Nepal, but she probably commissioned it at a workshop in northern India.The Buddha's robe on this image has been left plain, without pleat lines to obscure the beauty of the contours of the body.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Around the time when this sculpture was made, portable bronzes began to replace relics as the principal sacred commodity circulating in the Buddhist world.

title: Madonna Nursing the Christ Child
medium: pen and brown ink and brush and brown wash over red and black chalk, with traces of white; framing lines in pen and brown ink

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2468x3400px open-access image (region x=0.4599, y=0.7541, w=0.299, h=0.1626)

description: One of the finest of the rare drawings by Murillo, this sheet is a study for Virgin and Child, commissioned for the family chapel of the Marques de Santiago in Madrid and now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Prized today for their dynamism, Murillo’s drawings served the practical purpose of working out the positions of the figures.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: The inscription Morillo on this drawing is not the artist's signature but rather a notation likely made by a 17th-century owner of the drawing.

title: Tobias Healing His Father's Blindness
medium: Pen and brown ink, touched with white gouache; framing lines in pen and brown ink

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2863x3400px open-access image (region x=0.218, y=0.6479, w=0.4209, h=0.2668)

description: This drawing is a prime example of the Dutch painter Rembrandt van Rijn's innovative approach to biblical narrative, in which he often humanized traditional pictorial formulas through the inclusion of observed details from everyday life.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: The seated figure in this drawing is receiving cataract surgery on his left eye, a procedure pioneered in Amsterdam in 1635 by Dr. Job Janszoon van Meekren.

title: Point Judith, Rhode Island

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x1891px open-access image (region x=0.6959, y=0.2586, w=0.2, h=0.2697)

description: One of only a handful of nocturnal scenes painted by Heade, this evocative painting captures the effects of glimmering moonlight on land, sea, and sky. Although the artist depicts a specific location, his nighttime rendering shrouds most details in shadow, imparting a greater sense of mood than place. Human presence manifests itself through two sailing ships on the left side of the composition.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Home to Point Judith, the beach town of Narragansett has its population double during summertime.

title: Shakyamuni Emerging from the Mountains
alternativeTitles: Sakyamuni Coming Down from the Mountains

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 1518x3400px open-access image (region x=0.1726, y=0.4709, w=0.2991, h=0.1)

description: Shakyamuni emerged from the mountains after years of ascetic practices, which anticipated his sermon in Deer Park and attainment of enlightenment under the bodhi tree. However, this figure of Shakyamuni can be interpreted as having already achieved enlightenment and reentered the earthly world to spread the dharma (Buddhist law).
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: The painting was inscribed by the abbot of Jingde Temple 景德寺 of Mount Tiantong 天童山 near Ningbo 寧波.

title: Funerary Portrait of a Young Girl

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 1770x3400px open-access image (region x=0.2401, y=0.1376, w=0.3, h=0.1168)

description: Transforming the spirit—not beautifying the mortal body—may have been the purpose of adding golden lips and jewelry to this painting. Egyptian-style burial customs and arts persisted throughout Greek, Roman, and Byzantine rule over Egypt (305 BCE–641 CE). The woman depicted in this panel lived between cultures.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
tags: Egyptian and Ancient Near Eastern Art
interestingFacts: This painting can be dated based on the hairstyle popular at the end of the reign of Emperor Tiberius (reigned 14–37 CE).

title: Vase with Golden Pheasants
medium: porcelain painted in polychrome enamels over transparent glaze
culture: China, Jiangxi province, Jingdezhen kilns, Qing dynasty (1644-1911), Qianlong mark and period (1736-95)

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2267x3400px open-access image (region x=0.4248, y=0.6832, w=0.3, h=0.15)

description: The flower-and-bird painting in this vase was intricately executed in colored enamels (falangcai), with careful modeling, shading, and blending of colors reflecting European influences through missionary-artists at the Qing court. The Jesuit artist Giuseppe Castiglione (1688–1766), in particular, exerted tremendous impact at the Qianlong academy.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
tags: China, Jiangxi province, Jingdezhen kilns, Qing dynasty (1644-1911), Qianlong mark and period (1736-95)
interestingFacts: Refined porcelains produced in Jingdezhen kilns were sent to Beijing palace workshops to be decorated in falangcai technique under direct imperial supervision.

title: Terminus, the Device of Erasmus

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x3346px open-access image (region x=0.3291, y=0.4871, w=0.3, h=0.2289)

description: In the spirit of the Italian Renaissance, Erasmus of Rotterdam (c. 1466–1536), the celebrated Dutch humanist and scholar, embraced ancient Greek and Roman literature and incorporated much of its moral and ethical messages into his own work. Holbein here conflates Erasmus’s features with Terminus, the Roman god of boundaries, who defied Jupiter by maintaining his position atop Capitoline Hill.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Tree ring analysis helped determine the date of this painting.

title: Priest-King or Deity
medium: basalt with bone eyes (left, ancient; right, restored)

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 1412x3400px open-access image (region x=0.216, y=0.3603, w=0.3017, h=0.0938)

description: The Hittites migrated into Anatolia in the 3rd millennium BCE and spoke an Indo-European language, a group that includes Greek, Latin, Persian, Sanskrit, English, and most modern European languages. They were the first ancient people to use iron for weapons. From about 1600–1200 BCE their empire was at its peak, extending from central Anatolia to Syria, and south along the eastern Mediterranean.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
tags: Egyptian and Ancient Near Eastern Art
interestingFacts: The left eye of the sculpture is the original bone inlay while the right eye is a modern restoration done after the piece was damaged.

title: Portrait of a Woman

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2647x3400px open-access image (region x=0.2735, y=0.7291, w=0.3003, h=0.175)

description: Bronzino was court painter to Cosimo I de’Medici, the Duke of Florence. Though the woman cannot be definitively identified, she was likely affiliated with the Medici court. As in most of the portraits in this gallery, Bronzino emphasizes wealth, status, and courtly refinement above personality or individualized expression.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)

title: Hermine Gallia
medium: black chalk with graphite on light brown laid paper

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2389x3400px open-access image (region x=0.365, y=0.4291, w=0.2997, h=0.1582)

description: Gustav Klimt created this drawing in preparation for a painted portrait, now in the collection of the National Gallery, London. Both depict Hermine Gallia, née Hamburger, who belonged to a wealthy Jewish family in Vienna. Through vanguard circles in the city, she met the artist and commissioned a canvas of her own likeness.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: This drawing is one of about 40 drawings made by Gustav Klimt for his painted portrait of Hermine Gallia.

title: Branch Hill Pond, Hampstead
artistBio: With Turner, his exact contemporary, John Constable defined the parameters of genius for a generation of romantic landscape painters. The son of a prosperous miller and gentleman farmer, he entered into his profession late and was basically self-taught.

artistBioSource.name: Cleveland Museum of Art — artist biography

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x2629px open-access image (region x=0.4459, y=0.469, w=0.2, h=0.194)

description: An amateur meteorologist, John Constable was most at home painting meticulously observed cloud formations, weather conditions, and natural light effects. He believed an accurate rendering of these constantly shifting elements could convey his vision of the vitality and magnificence of the English countryside.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: In 1820, Constable found a retreat in Hampstead where he completed 100 studies of cloud formations, referring to the process as "skying."

title: Bust of a Chinese

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2714x3400px open-access image (region x=0.5041, y=0.4668, w=0.3003, h=0.1791)

description: This bust is related to the allegorical figure of Asia in Carpeaux's monumental bronze fountain, The Four Parts of the World Upholding the Celestial Sphere, commissioned by Baron Haussmann in 1867 for the Luxembourg Gardens in Paris. The figure was changed into a woman in the fountain and reflects the artist's interest in accurately portraying different ethnic groups. This bust exists in various sizes and media.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Greatly admired during his time, Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux received important commissions from French Emperor Napoleon III and Baron Georges-Eugène Haussmann.

title: Summer Night; Winter Day
medium: Pair of six-panel folding screens, ink, gold, and silver on paper

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 3400x3150px open-access image (region x=0.4126, y=0.4956, w=0.2, h=0.1622)

description: Ōkyo painted these panoramas in the summer of 1784. Regarded as Kyoto's most important painting teacher and accomplished artist, he had studied Western painting techniques, "realistic" sketching from nature, and traditional Japanese style painting (yamato-e). The naturalistic quality of these scenes results from a blend of detailed observation of nature and a remote, even detached regard for man's place in the world.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)

title: Yoga Narashimha, Vishnu in his Man-Lion Avatar

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2582x3400px open-access image (region x=0.6565, y=0.4418, w=0.2006, h=0.1147)

description: Narasimha means “man-lion” in Sanskrit, and is the name of one of the ten main avatars, or incarnations, of the Hindu god Vishnu. For devotees, the man-lion form recalls a myth that describes his superhuman defeat of a seemingly invincible demonic foe. This rare iconic form also embodies royal power and yogic discipline.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: The two posts on either side are for holding a halo that once encircled the figure.

title: Still Life with Herrings

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2754x3400px open-access image (region x=0.203, y=0.5918, w=0.3007, h=0.1832)

description: Chardin reflected intensely on the act of observation. Still life became a forum for sophisticated performances in paint, and his complex technique—he famously worked in private—uses a staggering combination of delicate glazes and roughly dragged thick paint to capture the varied surfaces, atmospheres, and spaces in this humble pantry shelf.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)

title: Matsumoto Koshiro IV as Gorobei, the Fish Seller from Sanya
alternativeTitles: Matsumoto Koshiro IV as Gorobei, the Fishmonger of Sanya

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2204x3400px open-access image (region x=0.0803, y=0.0897, w=0.1992, h=0.0979)

description: Sharaku portrayed the actor Matsumoto Koshiro IV in his role as the fish merchant Gorobei in the play A Medley of Tales of Revenge, performed at the Kiri Theater in June 1794. The actor specialized in the wagoto, or "gentle style," of acting. In the play, the fish merchant, whose business is located near the Yoshiwara, helps two courtesan sisters avenge their father’s murder.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)

title: Catching Fireflies Beneath a Willow Tree (center)

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2373x3400px open-access image (region x=0.3312, y=0.3541, w=0.3013, h=0.1582)

description: Caught up in a frenzied pursuit of fireflies, one boy has waded into a stream after his quarry, while a younger one watches in anticipation as a young woman thrusts her fan into the air in the hope of capturing hers. In the center of the composition, a girl examines the insects trapped in her elegantly carved cage.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: A sense of movement is conveyed by their sleeves fluttering in the breeze.

title: People of Japan in Light Verse (Kyōka)

description: The color woodcuts of Katsushika Hokusai were highly esteemed. One of his most famous prints, The Great Wave off Kanagawa (1823-31), is a striking image of an enormous cresting wave. Maillol exploited the curling water motif to achieve an energetic linear design that surrounds and cushions the nude woman but also creates a lively contrast to the large, flat white shape of her body.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: This print dates from a period when Aristide Maillol used his wife, Clotilde, as his primary model.

title: Portrait of Lisa Colt Curtis

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 1605x3400px open-access image (region x=0.3807, y=0.2626, w=0.4206, h=0.1479)

description: One of the most sought-after painters of his era, Sargent achieved considerable critical and financial success portraying cosmopolitan members of high society on both sides of the Atlantic. Here, the artist depicts an acquaintance—a relative of the Colt firearms family—who had recently married his distant cousin Ralph.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Although known as John Singer Sargent today, he almost never used his middle name during his lifetime.

title: Portrait of Tieleman Roosterman

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2529x3400px open-access image (region x=0.2661, y=0.0918, w=0.2997, h=0.1668)

description: An extremely wealthy linen and silk merchant in Haarlem, Tieleman Roosterman was 36 years old when Frans Hals painted his portrait. Unlike many Dutch painters of the period, Hals favored strong, visible brushstrokes that convey the vitality of his sitters.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
interestingFacts: Roosterman may have ordered this portrait--and one of his wife--to commemorate their wedding in 1631.

title: Head of Caracalla
medium: Red chalk on cream laid paper

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2655x3400px open-access image (region x=0.4972, y=0.6291, w=0.2004, h=0.1168)

description: As part of their training in the late 18th century, French artists practiced drawing têtes d'expression, or expressive heads, that display subtleties of human emotion. Greuze made this chalk study in preparation for a painting in which the Roman emperor Septimius Severus rebukes his notoriously ruthless son, Caracalla, for attempting to assassinate him.
license: CC0 1.0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)

title: Tomb Guardian with Animal Head
culture: China, probably Shaanxi province, Xi'an, Tang dynasty (618-907)

detail.source: Real crop of the museum's 2354x3400px open-access image (region x=0.3161, y=0.2541, w=0.3012, h=0.1562)

description: With their fierce expressions and exaggerated physical features, fantastic guardian creatures were intended to guard the entrance to a tomb, warding off evil as well as keeping the soul of the deceased from wandering.
